## [2026-09-17] ingest | Brad Gerstner: No AI Bubble, Semis Eat the Nasdaq & AI's Take Off Problem

Added source note for the All-In solo market check with Brad Gerstner. Key claims: the 2026 rally is framed as earnings-driven rather than a 2000-style bubble because earnings rose about 26% while Nasdaq, S&P, SOX and Nvidia multiples contracted; semiconductors account for roughly 70% of the Nasdaq's return, with token makers paid and token buyers "going along for the ride"; monthly revenue at Anthropic and OpenAI is the market's key variable, with the leading labs near a $100B run rate needing at least $180B by year end and offtake revenue growing toward $450B and then $800B-$1T against nearly $1.5T of annual capex; and the named risks are rates, electricity (a roughly 25-gigawatt expectation against a 43-gigawatt forecast) and regulation, with a medium, no-leverage positioning conclusion. Added concept pages for AI offtake revenue gap, semiconductor index concentration, and AI productivity margin expansion, and rewrote the Brad Gerstner entity page under the synthesis-v1 schema. Contradiction noted: the source qualifies the wiki's power-bottleneck branch by expecting the gigawatt buildout to undershoot while revenue targets are still met, and it is in tension with the bubble checklists that treat scarce late-stage AI valuations as euphoria evidence. All lab run rates, Anthropic revenue figures, gigawatt forecasts, and several garbled company names remain source-scoped.
